milestone: Austin/EXP-P1 reviewer experience closed: the IRL OS Workspace now projects Instrument Validation (IRV-001/IPV-001), Track 2 state, Crystal inspection, and Independent Review/Observer Review into the reviewer-facing Workspace surface, gated by the existing capability-ladder system (services/research/accessCapabilities.ts, shipped 2026-10-01) rather than a parallel reviewer UI or resolver. Filed at close-out per CLAUDE.md's Resolution -> Invariant Loop, triggers #7 (a successful implementation established a reusable pattern) and #8 (a milestone became demonstrably complete).
problem: An invited reviewer (e.g. Austin, holding a research-lab 'reviewer' grant scoped to EXP-P1) could appear entitled to a Workspace, but the Workspace projection (WorkspaceCapabilitiesPanel.tsx / GET /api/participation/workspace-capabilities) exposed only readiness, reviewer-kit documents, and the review-agreement countersignature -- not the Instrument Validation evidence, Track 2 programme state, Crystal readiness/provenance/receipts, or the Independent Review/Observer Review machinery the reviewer had actually been granted access to inspect. Several of the underlying Laboratory GET routes were ALSO admin-only despite having no mutation risk, which would have blocked the fix even after the Workspace panel was extended.
observedFailure: GET /api/research/track2/[experimentId] (Track 2 programme state) required persona.cartridgeFlags.isAdmin outright -- a scoped reviewer received 403 on the read path, not merely on mutation.

GET /api/research/crystal/[experimentId]/rehearsal (internal rehearsal lineage/results) and GET /api/research/crystal/[experimentId]/freeze (frozen artifact hashes/receipts, next governed action) were likewise admin-only reads, even though the sibling GET /api/research/crystal/[experimentId] (readiness/statistics/freeze recommendation) had already been correctly loosened to admit a scoped reviewer via callerMayReadExperimentReview.

No caller anywhere computed 'the highest ordinary capability rung (read/review/write/run) this persona holds at this resource' -- every existing caller of resolveCapability checked exactly one literal capability value (e.g. 'run'), which is correct for a single mutation gate but left the Workspace projection and any future UI/MCP surface with no single source of truth for which ladder rung to render or report.
rootCauses: The 2026-09-08 IRL OS Workspace consolidation and the 2026-10-01 capability-ladder system were both built correctly but had not yet been composed: the Workspace projection route was extended with new experiment-bound sections only up to the point OCSGA/EXP-P1 needed (readiness, documents, review agreement), and several Laboratory GET routes were written admin-only before the reviewer-read admission check (callerMayReadExperimentReview) existed as an established pattern, then never revisited once it did.
resolution: Loosened four READ-ONLY routes to admit isAdmin OR callerMayReadExperimentReview, the SAME check already used by the sibling Crystal readiness route and the readiness dashboard route: GET /api/research/track2/[experimentId]/route.ts, GET /api/research/crystal/[experimentId]/rehearsal/route.ts, and GET /api/research/crystal/[experimentId]/freeze/route.ts (the fourth sibling, instrument-falsification, was found already correctly loosened). Every mutating route beneath these (Track 2 merge/promote/reconcile/accept-bridges/relationship- and provenance-cohort/validate-all/suggest-relationships/diversity-candidates/relationship-adjudication; Crystal freeze POST, rehearsal POST, execution-rehearsal POST) was left untouched -- admin-only or resolveCapability('run')-gated exactly as before.

Added resolveEffectiveExperimentCapability (services/research/accessCapabilities.ts) -- the ONE cascade helper ('run' > 'write' > 'review', else 'read') any human UI, MCP tool, or future delegated-agent surface calls to render/report a persona's effective ordinary-ladder rung at one resource, rather than re-deriving the cascade per caller. High-risk capabilities remain explicitly OUT of this cascade, per the module's own existing discipline.

Extended GET /api/participation/workspace-capabilities and WorkspaceCapabilitiesPanel.tsx with four new experiment-bound sections -- Instrument Validation (mounts the existing, already read-only InstrumentValidationPanel for IRV-001/IPV-001), Track 2 state (a new, deliberately minimal READ-ONLY summary, Track2StateSummary.tsx, reading the loosened canonical GET route -- NOT a reviewer-mode retrofit of the ~7,000-line admin Track2ProgrammePanel, which was judged too large to safely retrofit in this pass and is named below as a remaining gap), and Crystal + Independent Review (mounts the existing CrystalObserverReviewPanel, which already composes IndependentReviewPanel reviewerMode with the self-service Observer Review decision submission -- built 2026-08-01/2026-09-08 for exactly this reviewer-safe purpose and reused unchanged). A capability badge (read/review/write/run/admin) renders from the server-resolved effectiveCapability field, never inferred client-side.

Bootstrapped the real acceptance-test grant: an access_grant_capabilities row (capability='review', scope_type='experiment', scope_ref='EXP-P1') was attached to the real, pre-existing 'Brozi' (Austin) research-lab reviewer grant (19d67c72-2194-45ab-8310-c48fba242c32) so this pass could verify against a live principal rather than only a fake/mocked one -- verified via direct read of the live access_grants/access_grant_capabilities tables (no SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY was available in this session's local environment to invoke the real TS functions end-to-end; verification composed live-DB inspection of the exact rows resolveCapability/resolveEffectiveExperimentCapability query, plus unit tests exercising the real functions against an equivalent fake dataset).
rejectedApproaches: Retrofitting a full reviewerMode into Track2ProgrammePanel (~7,000 lines, dozens of mutation controls: duplicate-pair merge, promotion, reconciliation, relationship/provenance cohorts, diversity/bridge candidates, validate-all) and mounting it directly in Workspace -- rejected for this pass as too large to audit for completeness within the available time without risking an unaudited mutation control being missed; every mutating Track 2 route is independently admin-gated regardless (server-side security is not weakened by this deferral), but the UI-level 'looks read-only, not broken' requirement is only partially met via the smaller Track2StateSummary substitute. Named explicitly as outstanding, not silently done partially.

Deriving 'effective capability' by checking resolveCapability once per specific value inline at each call site (as every existing caller already did for its own single gate) -- rejected in favor of one shared resolveEffectiveExperimentCapability helper, so the Workspace projection, any future UI, and MCP/agent parity all compute the SAME cascade rather than three independent re-derivations that could silently drift apart (inv.engineering.036/037).

Minting a fabricated HTTP session/bearer token to simulate Austin literally hitting the deployed routes through a browser -- rejected; no real credential for the 'Brozi' principal was available in this session, and fabricating a login flow result would violate this repo's No-Guessing rule. Verification instead composed direct, real-database inspection of the exact rows the authorization functions query, plus unit tests against the real functions with an equivalent seeded fake dataset -- the gap between this and a literal authenticated HTTP walkthrough is named explicitly rather than glossed over.
